questions: Has the right eyelid drooping and double vision come on suddenly, over hours to days?
Are you diabetic, or do you have high blood pressure?
Did the onset of these symptoms include severe pain around the eye or head?
Have you noticed any other neurological symptoms, such as weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking?
Has the right pupil always been smaller than the left, or have you only recently noticed?
Do you sweat normally on both sides of your face, or is the right side of your face drier?
Have you ever had any surgery or trauma to your neck, chest, or upper spine on the right side?
Do you ever get flushing or redness that is more pronounced on the left side of your face than the right?
Are you a smoker, or have you ever smoked?
Do you suffer from migraines or cluster headaches?
Have you recently had an ear infection, ear pain, or any change in your hearing?
Have you noticed any hoarseness or change in your voice, or difficulty swallowing?
Has the drooping of your right eyelid and the double vision gradually worsened over weeks, months, or years?
Do you have any numbness, tingling, or loss of sensation on the right side of your face or forehead?
Have you noticed any swelling, bulging, or change in the appearance of your right eye?
Does the double vision become significantly worse toward the end of the day or when you are tired?
Have you noticed any change in your vision or blurriness specifically in the right eye recently?
Is the bulging of the right eye something that has been developing over a long time, or did it happen quickly?
Have you ever been diagnosed with any thyroid problems, such as an overactive or underactive thyroid?
Have you ever had any cancer, or been told you have a tumor anywhere in your body?
Have you had any recent viral illness, vaccination, or febrile illness before these symptoms started?
Have you ever had any neurological condition such as multiple sclerosis, myasthenia gravis, or Guillain-Barré syndrome?
Is the right pupil smaller than the left pupil in dim lighting?
Is the right pupil larger than the left pupil in dim lighting?
orders: Examine the patient for relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD) in both eyes
Measure visual acuity in both eyes
Examine the optic disc appearance in both eyes
Assess ocular motility in all cardinal positions of gaze
Perform a cocaine 4% eyedrops test to differentiate preganglionic from postganglionic Horner's syndrome
Perform a hydroxyamphetamine 1% eyedrops test to differentiate preganglionic from postganglionic Horner's syndrome
MRI brain with contrast and thin slices through the brainstem
MR angiography of the head and neck to assess for aneurysm or dissection
